title: Chapter 2. The Account of Virachandra's Appearance
html:
Praise of Nityananda; Virachandra is born to Vasudha; Abhirama and Advaita recognize Gauranga in the infant; the gods come to see him (pp. 27–30)

[p. 27]

1Glory, glory to Prabhu Nityananda-Balarama!
Give me shelter at your feet and fulfil my desire.

2It is also said1:
"[He] whose form is honoured by the crimson rays of morning,
who, raising up what is called prema-bhakti, spread victory through the whole world."

3Glory, glory to Nityananda, glory to the Merciful One!
To me, most sinful, give, Prabhu, shelter at your feet.

4Refrain2:
Glory, glory to Nityananda, the Great Lord,
the support of all lords3!
Ocean of all rasas, beloved of the people of Vraja,
the second incarnation of Krishna!

5Husband of Vasu[dha]-Revati4, together with Jahnava
he bears the body of both purusha and prakriti.
He dwells in Gaura's heart, steeped in the mood dear to him,
ceaselessly sporting with Gaura.

6The world is smeared with the filth of Kali, the taste of Hari no longer shines,
for Gaura Gosani has passed from sight.
Without pure bhakti, by any other worship,
the people of Kali have no other way.

7If merciful Krishna, pitying the poor and destitute,
descends once more as an incarnation,
then, showing mercy again to all living beings,
he delivers them.

8Vasudha and Jahnava Devi, serving the god Narayana,
by their pure, sattvic minds are worthy to be honoured [with their feet] upon the head.
Beloved of Nityananda, gracious mistresses,
[honoured] by all women5.

9Her womb is like the Milk Ocean,
[from which] Virachandra appeared6.
O virtuous friends, fix it in your minds:
Krishna has made himself known7.

10To destroy the filth of Kali, Virachandra
is [like Yama] to the wicked of the earth8.
Endowed with the thirty-two marks, a splendid man,
he shines like the sun even without ornaments.

[p. 28]

11Nityananda-chandra, overjoyed,
laughs loud and long.
The minds and lives of all people are surely won over,
says Vrindavana Dasa.

12The Lord never has birth and deeds [as humans do];
the Vedas speak only of his appearance and disappearance.

13This transcendent lila is for the deliverance of souls;
in this human lila [the Lord] appears worldly.

14Who but the devotees can understand this lila?
Who knows what the Lord's inconceivable power will do, and when?

15Waiting for an auspicious day, an auspicious lagna and an auspicious moment,
knowing his own word to be unfailing9,

16on the ninth day of the dark fortnight of autumn, on a purifying day,
the Lord appeared, and the whole world floated in bliss.

17Through the three worlds rang "Jaya, jaya!" and the sound of Hari's name;
the world of gods and the world of men floated in bliss.

18"Blessed, blessed is Vasu-Lakshmi!" said everyone.
"She has borne a son — that very Gaura-Narayana."

19She who for fifteen months carried [him] in a form of radiance
gave birth on the fourth day of the bright fortnight of Margashirsha10.

20On this, a song sung in the raga11:
In radiance a golden lotus, the curves of his body most lovely,
his arms reaching to his knees.
His waist is slender as a lion's or a dambaru drum,
on his chest […] shines12.

21His lotus feet are most beautiful, marked with the flag, thunderbolt and goad;
even the red lotus is not so fine13.
Sweetly, sweetly he smiles, pouring out streams of nectar;
whoever sees him is purified in heart.

22All the ladies of good families come and, smiling at the sight of the boy,
praise him: "Blessed, blessed!
Fortunate is Vasu-Lakshmi, the virtuous one, who has borne a son —
the enchanter of the world, how wonderful!"

23Seeing the boy, all are amazed:
"This is surely some mahapurusha!"
Vrindavana Dasa says: this is no worldly child,
this is the complete, eternal Brahman.

24In the form of Virachandra Gaura has descended again:
whoever has not seen Gaurachandra, let him see him once more.

25Enchanter of the world, he plays in the form of a child
and grows day by day like the crescent moon.

26One day Prabhu14 was sitting outside,
when Abhirama arrived in haste.

27At the door he called out, "Dada Balai!"15
and, coming into the courtyard, again laughed a great deal.

28Nityananda ran and embraced him round the neck,
and Abhirama speaks very sweetly:

29"I have heard that a child has been born to you.
Show him to me — I will bow down to him."

30Nityananda replies: "You know it all yourself.
I do not even know who has come from where."

31Thus the two speak to each other in hints
and, embracing, weep with love.

32Vasu Devi, hearing that Abhirama had come,
thinks to herself: "What will Krishna do?"16

33"I have heard that, prostrating before deities,
he has split them in many places on his way here."

34Virachandra was lying on a little bed,
holding a piece of divine red cloth to his chest.

[p. 29]

35The pupils of his eyes are half closed,
like bees at dusk sinking into the cups of lotuses.

36By his ears is a bright line of kohl,
in the middle of his forehead a dot of cow dung17.

37On his lovely hair a forelock is set in front;
whoever beholds it, it awakens in his heart.

38Vasu-Lakshmi lifted her son and took him on her lap,
and just then Abhirama came there.

39Seeing [him], Vasu-Lakshmi gave [the son] onto Jahnava's lap,
and the Devi joyfully took the son on her lap.

40The mother stroked the boy's head,
and Prabhu smiles gently, looking at his mother.

41Just then Abhirama came there18
and, unblinking, stood gazing at the infant's form.

42It was as if a nectar salve touched his eyes:
all his senses were soothed as he beheld [the child].

43Prabhu lies at ease on his mother's lap,
as though the rays of dawn had entered the house.

44A high nose and a lovely forehead,
mighty arms, a long body, a broad chest.

45His palms and soles look as if rubbed with vermilion19,
and on them are the marks of a mahapurusha.

46Seeing this, Abhirama rejoiced,
went to his feet and bowed down.

47Rising, he gazed at him and prostrated again —
again and again, three times he did so.

48Waking from yoga-nidra, Prabhu smiles
and, kicking his feet, becomes just like an infant.

49Abhirama recognized him: "This is my Lord!"
And, laughing, he says: "Fine lordly tricks of yours!"

50As Gauranga's beauty was lovely before,
so is the whole body of Virachandra.

51The same radiance of the moonlike face, the same two eyes,
the same two arms reaching to the knees.

52The same curves of the whole body. Seeing this, Abhirama
says, "It is he, it is he!" and both his eyes stream with love.

53Circling him and prostrating again,
floating in the bliss of love, he cries, "Hari, Hari!"

54Playing horn and flute, he went outside;
Nityananda seated him with honour.

55A crest of peacock feathers, a garland of gunja and flowers,
makara earrings in his ears, bangles on his arms.

56Bells and a dhoti at his waist, anklets on his feet;
his body the colour of ketaki, his build graceful.

57Sridama, son of King Vrishabhanu —
that same perfected cowherd boy, now named only "Abhirama"20.

58Having stayed one night, he went on to another place;
in longing and in bliss he wanders, never resting.

59Under the guise of childhood play Prabhu reveals himself
and sports, giving joy to Nityananda-chandra.

60Advaita Gosani came from Shantipur;
seeing [the child] he rejoiced, but kept his guard:

61"The thief has come again — into the house of the caste-breaker21:
now he is an avadhuta, now he lives in household life."

62By the power of bhakti Sitanatha22 knew:
this is that same Prabhu Gaurachandra in person.

[p. 30]

63"The thief from the thieves' house steals every day —
how are we to catch this thief?"

64Advaita Gosani is by nature skilled in tarja23;
only one to whom he shows mercy grasps its full meaning.

65Knowing him to be the Lord of his life, Advaita Gosani
bowed many times, beside himself with love.

66"That same thief! That same thief!" says Advaita.
Who will grasp the truth of all these words of love?

67Seeing this, everyone wondered in their hearts:
"What mahapurusha has come to Nityananda's house?"

68Circling [the child], Advaita went home,
and all the other foremost Vaishnavas went to their homes.

69Thus Virachandra, in the guise of a child,
performs charming play day after day.

70How can I describe the sweetness of Virachandra's beauty?
Wherever one's eyes fall, there they stay, gazing.

71His loveliness, like that of millions of Kandarpas, enchants the mind;
Brahma and the other gods come to see him.

72Taking human form24, all the gods
come every day to behold Virachandra:

73"Fine play you perform, Prabhu, on earth!
Without your mercy who could know it?

74In the dreadful Kali age, Prabhu, you perform such play —
who can know that you are the independent Lord?"

75Thus the gods bow and praise him,
and Virachandra-Narayana, hearing it, laughs.

76Makara anklets on his feet, a tiger's claw at his neck;
did the Creator fashion his form from a blend of rasas?

77What to speak of others — Nityananda himself is enchanted
and never thinks of him as a son at all.

78Between Virachandra and Gaurachandra there is no difference:
the Vedas speak only of appearance and disappearance.

79Hoping for the feet of Sri Virachandra Gosani,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the Vamsha-vistara.

Thus ends, in the Adi-lila of the Vamsha-vistara of Sri Nityananda Prabhu, the second chapter, called "The Account of the Appearance of Srila Sriyukta Virachandra".

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. The Sanskrit line is badly corrupted in both copies ("prātaḥ semakarāruṇairvandīkṛta svavigrahaṁ / premabhaktyākhyamutsthāpya sañcārita jagajjaẏam"); the translation of the first half is conjectural. It apparently praises Virachandra (imagery of the moon or a luminary).
  2. "Dhuya" — the refrain of a song; what follows are tripadi stanzas, each under one number.
  3. "sakala īśvara ādhāra" reconstructed from two corrupt copies ("īkara āvāra" / "sakala bhāvāra"); the reading is conjectural.
  4. Revati is Balarama's consort; the poet identifies Vasudha with her. "jāhnavā saṁhati" (A "saṁsthati", B "saṁhṛti") is taken as "together with Jahnava".
  5. The copies read "vadhyā / vdhya", taken as "vandyā", "honoured".
  6. A play on the name: in the Puranas the moon (chandra) is born from the churning of the Milk Ocean; so Vira-"chandra" is born from Vasudha's womb.
  7. "kṛṣṇa karala paricāra" is unclear (in copy A the line is nearly lost); taken as "Krishna has made himself known".
  8. The copies read "vīracandra sama" ("like"); probably to be read "yama", "Yama to the wicked". The last line of the stanza ("ubharaṇa/ubhavaṇa vinā michira") is taken as "ābharaṇa vinā mihira", "a sun even without ornaments".
  9. That is, Gauranga's (Chaitanya's) promise to appear again, told in Chapter 1.
  10. The ninth day of the dark fortnight of autumn (probably the month of Ashvina) is apparently the day the Lord entered the womb; the fifteen-month pregnancy stresses the supernatural birth. Margashirsha (Agrahayana) is November–December.
  11. The name of the raga is not given in the text ("yathā rāgera gīẏate").
  12. The third part of the line is lost in copy A and corrupt in B ("e vakṣa kanṭa kiśorī virāje").
  13. "raktotpala aruṇa nahi bhāle" — a conjectural reconstruction from B ("vaktopala aru nahi bhāle").
  14. Here "Prabhu" is Nityananda.
  15. Dada, "elder brother"; Balai, an affectionate name of Balarama. Abhirama addresses Nityananda as Balarama.
  16. According to tradition, Abhirama's obeisance was unbearable to anyone who was not a genuine incarnation: Nityananda's sons born before Virachandra died from it, and false deities cracked. Hence Vasudha's anxiety.
  17. A dot of cow dung on an infant's forehead is a charm against the evil eye.
  18. The line repeats couplet 38; so in the original.
  19. "māḍila liṅgule" taken as "māṛaila hiṅgule", "rubbed with vermilion".
  20. Sridama is Krishna's friend in Vraja, brother of Radha (daughter of Vrishabhanu). Abhirama Thakura is held to be his incarnation.
  21. "Caste-breaker" — a teasing name for Nityananda the avadhuta, who disregarded caste rules. The "thief" is Krishna, who "steals" hearts; Advaita hints that Gauranga has appeared again in the infant.
  22. Sitanatha, "Sita's husband", i.e. Advaita Acharya.
  23. Tarja (tarajā; the copies read "taṅjāẏa/bhaṅjāẏa") — riddling, allusive verses; Advaita is known for his tarja addressed to Chaitanya.
  24. The copies read "navarūpa" ("a new form"); probably "nararūpa", "human form".
